title: Field hit-targets and dynamic focus heuristics for composed inputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Audit and define concrete interaction rules and token guidance for composed input controls (text fields with prefix/suffix affordances, selects with clear buttons, toggles inline with inputs), with particular focus on: hit target size for mouse and touch, focus ring behavior in dense variants, pointer-event layering for overlapping affordances, and accessible keyboard flow. Outcome: a set of token changes, component API recommendations, and two implementation tickets for engineering to implement in runtime and console components.
background: Multiple recent product requests and support escalations show inconsistent behavior across dense and regular input variants when inputs include inline actions (clear, reveal, dropdown chevron, toggle). Users on touch devices report missed taps; keyboard users report focus landing on small interactive affordances out of expected order. Current tokens for input padding and hit targets were defined years ago for non-composed inputs and haven't been reconciled with dense UI patterns or the compact density tokens introduced last year.
goals: Define an explicit hit-target policy that balances visual compactness with touch accessibility for both mouse and touch users
Create deterministic focus heuristics for composed inputs so keyboard focus order and ring visibility are consistent
Propose token updates and component props for inputs, selects, and toggle-adjacent-controls to make implementation straightforward
Document trade-offs and migration plan so teams can adopt without regressions
scope: Text input (single-line) with prefix/suffix icons or action buttons
Selects that include inline clear and chevron affordances
Toggle/switches placed inline or adjacent to inputs
Dense and regular density variants defined in the design token set
Accessibility: keyboard order, ARIA labeling, and touch target minimums
out_of_scope: Complete visual redesign of inputs (color/typography changes unrelated to hit targets)
Platform-specific native mobile SDK changes (investigate only)
acceptance_criteria: A1: For both dense and regular variants, every interactive affordance inside or adjacent to an input has a 40px minimum touch target in CSS while allowing visual reduction when necessary (visual 24px vs hit target 40px via invisible padding or pseudo-elements)

A2: Focus ring behavior: when tabbing into a composed field, keyboard focus lands first on the text field, then sequentially on left-to-right inline affordances; visible focus ring meets contrast requirements for high-contrast themes
A3: Token changes produced: spacing.input.padding.{regular,dense}, control.touch_min_size, component.input.affordance_margin, with migration notes for legacy tokens
A4: Provide component API recommendations (e.g., input.prop: affordanceMode = [compact|overlap|spaced], ariaUsage guidance) and example code snippets for React SDK
A5: Design spec in Figma and Confluence doc linked; engineering tickets created and accepted into next cycle for implementation (ENG-1987 dependency acknowledged)
A6: Cross-browser test plan documented (desktop mouse, iOS Safari touch, Android Chrome touch) and manual QA checklist included
design_notes: Trade-off: prioritize 40px touch target for mobile even if it requires invisible padding for dense visual treatments. This keeps visual density while meeting a11y guidelines.

Introduce a pointer-capability-aware heuristic: when pointer:fine (mouse), allow tighter visual hit areas; when pointer:coarse (touch), apply expanded invisible padding. Document fallback for hybrid devices.
For composed fields with prefix icons + clear button, collapse visual spacing but maintain logical spacing for focus and touch via dedicated affordanceMargin token
Propose affordanceMode prop to allow components to opt into overlapping affordances for legacy compact forms (migration path), with default behavior being 'spaced' to ensure accessibility
engineering_notes: Implementation approach: prefer CSS-only solutions (padding + negative margin + hit-target pseudo-element) to avoid layout shifts. If not possible, small DOM wrapper allowed.

Edge case: inputs inside compact table rows where visual height is constrained <32px. Will provide an exception policy and a fallback to 'overlay' mode where affordances appear as hover overlays on pointer:fine devices only
Coordinate with runtime team to ensure prefix/suffix caching and KV pathing unaffected by wrapper elements (ENG-1987).
Provide unit and accessibility tests: keyboard order tests, focus-visible tests, touch target size checks via integration tests
decisions: Decided: Minimum interactive hit target enforced as 40px for touch-capable contexts. This is applied via invisible padding when visual size <40px.
Decided: Default focus order is input -> prefix actions (left to right) -> suffix actions -> external controls (e.g., adjacent toggle).
Decided: Introduce affordanceMode prop with values ['spaced', 'overlap', 'overlay'] and default to 'spaced' for accessibility by default.
Decided: Dense visual variant will keep reduced visual padding but must still satisfy touch target via invisible hit area for mobile contexts.
